# `aitbc eth transfers`

Fetch ETH transfers for the fleet's Sepolia wallets and append new rows to a JSONL log. Read-only and key-free: no wallet file, key, env file, ledger or database is touched. On a second run only rows not yet in the log are appended. Every wallet's outgoing transaction count is cross-checked against its RPC nonce; a mismatch warns and exits non-zero.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc eth transfers [OPTIONS] [ADDRESSES...]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `addresses` | text … | no | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--address`, `-a` | text (multiple) | — | no | Address or wallet label (repeatable) |
| `--since` | text | — | no | Only rows at/after this block number or UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--json` | flag | `false` | no | Emit the new rows as JSON |
| `--log` | file | `~/.aitbc/eth-transfers.jsonl` | no | JSONL transfer log |
| `--no-log` | flag | `false` | no | Print only; do not read or write the log |
| `--rpc-url` | text | `https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com` | no | Sepolia JSON-RPC endpoint |
| `--explorer-url` | text | `https://eth-sepolia.blockscout.com` | no | Blockscout-compatible explorer base URL |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc eth transfers
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc eth transfers --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
